recording consists of 8 channels with 8000 signal samples.\n\nTo convert the raw EMG signals into a format suitable for machine learning, nine statistical features are extracted from each channel:\n\n- Mean\n- Median\n- Standard Deviation\n- Minimum\n- Maximum\n- First Quartile (Q1)\n- Third Quartile (Q3)\n- Skewness\n- Kurtosis\n\nSince there are 8 channels, a total of **72 features (8 × 9)** are extracted for every recording.","metadata":{}},{"id":"fb6bcc17-6447-4b37-a4de-bf1484c39fb2","cell_type":"code","source":"# ============================================================\n# Task 2\n# Section 2.4 : Statistical Feature Extraction\n# ============================================================\n\nfrom scipy.io import loadmat\nfrom scipy.stats import skew, kurtosis\n\nfeature_list = []\n\nfor file in metadata_df[\"File\"]:\n\n    # Load EMG signal\n    signal = loadmat(file)[\"value\"]          # Shape: (8, 8000)\n\n    sample_features = []\n\n    # Extract features from each channel\n    for ch in signal:\n\n        sample_features.extend([\n            np.mean(ch),\n            np.median(ch),\n            np.std(ch),\n            np.min(ch),\n            np.max(ch),\n            np.percentile(ch, 25),\n            np.percentile(ch, 75),\n            skew(ch),\n            kurtosis(ch)\n        ])\n\n    feature_list.append(sample_features)\n\nprint(\"Feature extraction completed.\")","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-08-04T06:14:22.437710Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-08-04T06:14:22.438187Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-08-04T06:16:14.028915Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-08-04T06:14:22.438161Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-08-04T06:16:14.027821Z"}},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","text":"Feature feature_names.append(f\"Ch{ch}_{stat}\")\n\n# Create DataFrame\nstats_df = pd.DataFrame(feature_list, columns=feature_names)\n\nprint(\"=\" * 60)\nprint(\"FEATURE DATASET\")\nprint(\"=\" * masks\ntrain_mask = metadata_df[\"Subject\"].isin(train_subjects)\ntest_mask = metadata_df[\"Subject\"].isin(test_subjects)\n\n# Split dataset\nX_train = subject-independent train-test split. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and macro F1-score.\n\nAmong all evaluated models, **Gradient Boosting** and **LightGBM** achieved the highest classification accuracy (**57.22%**) and macro F1-score (**0.56**). **Random Forest** also demonstrated competitive performance with an accuracy of **56.11%**.\n\nTree-based ensemble methods consistently outperformed traditional classifiers such as Logistic Regression, k-NN, Decision Tree, and SVM, as well as the Multi-Layer Perceptron. This suggests that ensemble learning is particularly effective for the extracted statistical EMG features.\n\nBased on these results, **Gradient Boosting and LightGBM are selected as the strongest baseline models**, and the proposed Graph Neural Network (GNN) will be compared against these models in the subsequent experiments.","metadata":{}},{"id":"715120b4-86df-434b-9e24-e9d0466c2c7c","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 3.10 Bagging k-Nearest Neighbors (Bagging k-NN)\n\nBagging k-Nearest Neighbors (Bagging k-NN) is an ensemble learning approach that trains multiple k-NN classifiers on different bootstrap samples of the training data.
